name: Manage proppant and chemicals on a frac pad
summary: Over the days a pad is fractured, roughly 150 to 200 truckloads of frac sand in two or three mesh sizes arrive at the wellsite and must be checked, unloaded into storage units and fed to the blender in the order the stages need them. Sand operators check load tickets, direct unloading and track storage levels against the stage schedule, a proppant logistics coordinator at the base re-sequences carrier trucks around the clock, and blender operators receive and track chemical totes. If storage runs short pumping stops, if it is full trucks queue at the pad and run up standby charges, and paper load tickets have to be reconciled against what was pumped at the end of the pad.

baseline.org_archetype: A TSX-listed Canadian pressure pumping company with six to eight 24-hour frac crews working for producers in Alberta and northeast BC, run from district bases with a Calgary head office.
baseline.notes: Modelled on the organisation file oilfield-services-co (composite based on Trican and STEP Canada). 2020 was a deep downturn and sits at the low end of volume ranges.

unit_of_work: one pad (all proppant and chemicals received and reconciled for one multi-well pad)
trigger: The first proppant truck for the pad is dispatched by the last-mile hauling process, usually a day before the first stage so storage can be pre-loaded.
end_state: All proppant and chemicals for the pad are received, pumped or returned, leftovers are dealt with, and the reconciliation and signed load tickets are with the logistics coordinator and the district office.

volume.seasonality: Follows pads fractured: highest January to mid-March, near zero during spring break-up, steady over summer and fall.

surge.cause: Winter completion peak while frozen ground allows access to muskeg leases (January to mid-March)

evidence.note: Same surge as the organisation file's process map entry (crews fully booked January to mid-March); the multiplier is an estimate from quarterly proppant swings of 260,000-479,000 tonnes in the organisation file.

Organisation file process map volume (about three wells per pad at 50 wells a month). About 6,750 tonnes per pad at roughly 38-40 tonnes per truckload gives about 170 loads, consistent with the organisation file's estimate of about 3,000 sand truckloads a month.

Organisation file headcount 30; about 30% of time on receiving, unloading and tracking proppant (the share spent feeding the blender is in the job execution workflow; the rest is rig-up, rig-down and moves). Estimate.
Organisation file headcount 45; chemical receiving, storage and counts take a small share of time (estimate).
Organisation file headcount 14 (24x7 desk); about 13% of their time is wellsite re-sequencing for active pads, the rest is rail and terminal work in the supply chain processes (estimate).

systems.name: Dispatch and crew scheduling board (scheduling module, whiteboards, spreadsheets)
Vehicle telematics and electronic driver logs
Email, Microsoft Teams and mobile phones
ERP (finance, procurement, inventory, plant maintenance, billing)
HSE incident, hazard assessment and audit system

resources.name: Wellsite proppant storage and conveyor units
Highway tractor for pump, blender and bulk trailers

steps.name: Confirm storage readiness and the delivery plan
steps.description: The logistics coordinator calls the sand operator on location to confirm the storage units are spotted and empty, then checks the day-by-day delivery plan by mesh against the pad's stage schedule and the carriers booked for the first 24 hours.

error.defect_description: A mesh split or start time is out of date in the plan.

evidence.note: Last-mile dispatch runs around the clock and tracks inventory and wait times (Source Energy logistics page); times estimated.

steps.name: Inspect storage units, scales and dust collection
steps.description: Before the first load the sand operator checks the storage compartments are empty and dry, the conveyor belts, gates and load cells work, and the dust collectors are running, and assigns compartments to each mesh size.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code occupational exposure limit for respirable crystalline silica; company dust control procedure

evidence.note: Enclosed storage with dust collection to limit silica exposure (Source Energy Sahara page).

steps.name: Trucks deliver proppant through the pad
steps.description: Carrier trucks (super B-trains and pneumatic tankers) arrive in waves, first to pre-load storage and then to keep it topped up through the pumping days. Drivers wait in line on the lease road, back up to the storage unit and unload by gravity or air. The wait before this step stands for the delivery period of the pad, over which the receiving steps that follow are spread; drivers' own time is not company labour.

evidence.note: Over 300 third-party trucks dispatched for last-mile delivery; storage units take two trucks at once (Source Energy pages). Delivery period estimated as one day of pre-load plus about 2.2 pumping days per well.

steps.name: Check each load ticket against the order
steps.description: For every truck the sand operator reads the load ticket: supplier, terminal, mesh size, weight and the pad and well it is for, and compares it with the delivery plan before letting the driver unload. A load for the wrong mesh or pad is held.

error.defect_description: A load of the wrong mesh is accepted into the wrong compartment.

control.basis: Company receiving check: load ticket matched to the order before unloading; signed tickets support carrier invoices

evidence.note: About 170 loads at about 3 minutes each (estimate).

steps.name: Direct unloading into storage by mesh
steps.description: The sand operator guides each truck to the right unloading point, opens the compartment for that mesh, watches the fill level and stops the unload if the compartment is full, then waves the truck off the lease.

error.defect_description: Sand goes into a compartment holding another mesh.

evidence.note: About 170 loads at about 8 minutes of operator time each (estimate).

steps.name: Sign and file load tickets
steps.description: The sand operator signs the paper or electronic load ticket with the time unloaded and any wait time, keeps a copy in the binder for the pad and writes the load on the tally sheet.

error.defect_description: A ticket is lost, signed twice or tallied wrongly.

evidence.note: About 1.5 minutes a load (estimate).

steps.name: Track storage levels by mesh against the stage schedule
steps.description: Each shift the sand operator reads the compartment levels, subtracts what the next stages need by mesh from the treater's schedule and works out how many hours of each mesh are left.

error.defect_description: Inventory is over-counted and a mesh runs shorter than expected.

evidence.note: Storage units offer inventory monitoring (Source Energy Sahara page); many pads in 2019-2022 still used tally sheets and whiteboards. Time estimated.

steps.name: Update the logistics coordinator each shift
steps.description: The sand operator phones or texts the logistics coordinator with the inventory by mesh, trucks on location and the expected pumping rate, and flags any mesh that will run short or any queue building at the lease.

evidence.note: Two updates a day over about seven days (estimate).

steps.name: Re-sequence truck dispatch to match pumping
steps.description: The logistics coordinator compares the updates with trucks loading at the terminal and on the road, then speeds up, holds or reassigns trucks between pads on the dispatch board so storage neither runs dry nor overflows.

next.condition: a load is off-spec or the wrong mesh
a storm or road closure delays trucks

evidence.note: Dispatch monitors inventory and cycle wait times in real time (Source Energy logistics page). Branch shares are estimates.

steps.name: Hold trucks and log their standby time
steps.description: When storage is full the sand operator holds arriving trucks on the lease road, records arrival and unload times on each ticket for the carrier's standby (demurrage) charge, and tells the coordinator to slow dispatch.

error.defect_description: Standby times are not recorded and later disputed by the carrier.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Expedite loads and warn the treater
steps.description: The coordinator pulls trucks from other pads or calls extra carriers for the short mesh, and the sand operator warns the treater so the stage design can be adjusted or pumping held. If the sand does not arrive in time, pumping stops and the stoppage is logged as non-productive time.

evidence.note: Running short of sand stops pumping (organisation file process description); times estimated.

steps.name: Reject or quarantine a load and take a sample
steps.description: If a load is wet, contaminated, the wrong mesh or the wrong supplier, the sand operator refuses it or puts it in a separate compartment, takes a sample for the lab and photographs the ticket.

control.basis: Customer and company proppant quality specification by mesh and supplier

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Arrange a replacement load and the return
steps.description: The coordinator books a replacement truck for the right mesh and arranges for the rejected load to go back to the terminal, and notes the claim against the supplier or carrier.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Re-route trucks during a storm or road closure
steps.description: When snow, rain or a road closure slows trucks, the coordinator re-routes them, warns the field supervisor how long storage will last and may ask for pumping to slow until the roads open.

evidence.note: Weather delays reported in Canadian frac operations (STEP 2021); durations estimated.

steps.name: Receive chemical totes and check the delivery papers
steps.description: The blender operator receives totes of friction reducer, crosslinker, breaker, biocide and other additives, checks product names, lot numbers and quantities against the delivery and dangerous goods papers, and records them on the chemical sheet.

error.defect_description: A tote is recorded with the wrong product or lot.

control.basis: Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations: shipping documents checked on receipt

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Place totes in containment and label them
steps.description: The blender operator places totes in lined containment near the blender, checks WHMIS labels and safety data sheets are on site, and connects the totes in use to the liquid additive pumps.

error.defect_description: A tote is connected to the wrong additive line.

control.basis: WHMIS 2015 labelling and safety data sheets (Hazardous Products Act and Alberta OHS Code)

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Count chemical inventory and decide on top-ups
steps.description: Each shift the blender operator dips or weighs the totes, compares what is left with the chemical loadings for the remaining stages and decides whether more of any product is needed before the pad ends.

error.defect_description: A tote count is wrong and a product runs short.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Call for a hot-shot chemical delivery
steps.description: The blender operator calls the chemical blending plant or the frac coordinator for extra totes of the short product and tells the treater how many stages are left before it runs out.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Clean storage units and check dust exposure controls
steps.description: Between pads and during long pads the sand operator cleans spilled sand around the unloading points and conveyors, checks the dust collector filters and makes sure crew in the sand area wear respirators where required.

control.basis: Alberta OHS Code respirable crystalline silica exposure limit and respiratory protection requirements

evidence.note: Enclosed storage with dust collection to reduce silica exposure (Source Energy Sahara page).

steps.name: Draw storage down on the last well
steps.description: As the last well nears its final stages the sand operator and coordinator work out how much of each mesh is still needed and stop dispatch so as little sand as possible is left in storage at the end.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Arrange backhaul or transfer of leftover proppant
steps.description: The coordinator books trucks to move leftover sand to the next pad or back to the terminal and records the quantity so it is not billed to the customer.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile proppant received against pumped by mesh
steps.description: The sand operator adds up the signed load tickets by mesh, compares them with tonnes pumped from the data van and the leftover in storage, and lists any gap larger than one truckload.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Chase missing or disputed load tickets
steps.description: The coordinator asks carriers and the terminal for copies of missing tickets, compares scale weights and sorts out which loads were delivered to this pad.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile chemicals used and return unused totes
steps.description: The blender operator compares chemicals received with volumes used from the data van and the remaining totes, labels partly used totes for the next pad or return to the plant, and gives the chemical sheet to the treater for the field ticket.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Send the reconciliation and tickets to the base
steps.description: The logistics coordinator reviews the proppant and chemical reconciliations, files the signed load tickets for carrier invoice matching and sends the totals to the district office for the field ticket.

evidence.note: Estimate.

exceptions.name: Trucks queue at a full pad
exceptions.description: Storage is full and trucks wait, running up standby charges.

exceptions.name: Mesh runs short
exceptions.description: Loads are expedited; some cases stop pumping.

exceptions.name: Off-spec or wrong load
exceptions.description: A load is rejected and replaced.

exceptions.name: Weather or road delay
exceptions.description: Trucks are re-routed or slowed by storms or closures.

exceptions.name: Leftover proppant
exceptions.description: Sand is moved to the next pad or back to the terminal.

exceptions.name: Ticket gaps
exceptions.description: Missing or disputed tickets are chased with carriers.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from first truck dispatched to reconciliation sent

evidence.note: Derived: one day of pre-load, about 2.2 pumping days per well for three wells (STEP Canada 2021 tonnes per operating day and organisation file tonnes per well), and one to two days to reconcile.

pain_points.description: Storage holds only one to two days of pumping, so truck timing has to track the pumping rate closely; a slow day fills storage and trucks queue, a fast day or a road delay empties it.

evidence.note: 1,800-tonne storage units against about 1,040 tonnes pumped per operating day.

pain_points.description: Paper load tickets are signed at the pad and later matched by hand against tonnes pumped and carrier invoices; missing tickets take days to chase.

evidence.note: Common practice in 2019-2022; author's estimate of how often tickets go missing.

pain_points.description: Leftover proppant at the end of a pad has to be moved or written off.

evidence.note: Estimate.

sources.title: STEP Energy Services Ltd. Reports Fourth Quarter and Year End 2021 Results
sources.supports: Canadian fracturing 2021: 977 operating days and 1,012,000 tonnes of proppant (about 1,040 tonnes per operating day); 704 days and 776,000 tonnes in 2020; four spreads with 200,000 HP; Q4 2021 work hit by extended delays on a client location from challenging well conditions and by late-December weather; smaller jobs reduce proppant per day; spring break-up restricts equipment moves.

sources.title: Well Site Sand Storage (Sahara)
sources.supports: Wellsite proppant storage unit with 1,800 tonnes of capacity, unloading two trucks at once from any trailer configuration, fully enclosed with dust collection to limit silica exposure, real-time inventory monitoring; record of 6,155 tonnes supplied to the blender in a day.

sources.title: Last-Mile Logistics
sources.supports: WCSB last-mile proppant delivery with over 300 third-party trucks dispatched by a 24/7 dispatch team that monitors inventory, loading, unloading and cycle wait times; over 2.0 million tonnes of proppant and other materials delivered a year.

assumptions: Per-truck work (about 170 loads a pad) is summed into one step per activity. The pad's delivery period is entered as the wait before s03 (trucks arriving in waves over pre-load and pumping days) and the receiving steps s04-s09 are summed totals that in reality are spread over that period; the simulator adds them after it, which overstates elapsed time by roughly one day.
Feeding proppant from storage to the blender during pumping is counted in the job execution workflow, not here.
Truck payloads of about 38-40 tonnes are an estimate for super B-trains under Alberta weights; no source was opened for them.
The process is triggered per pad by the first proppant delivery; the delivery plan itself is made in the last-mile hauling process.
The logistics coordinator role sits in supply chain (organisation file); some companies keep a sand coordinator in the frac service line instead.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (base wage x 1.35).
